exp::short_text/aesthetic_001.source: The cello entered quietly beneath the orchestra, a single low note that swelled until it filled the concert hall like warm water rising. Several people in the audience closed their eyes. The note held for what felt like a full minute before resolving into a melody so tender it seemed to ache.

exp::short_text/aesthetic_001.back: From beneath the orchestra began the low sound of the cello, a solitary dim tone that resonated until it filled the concert hall like rising lukewarm water. Many in the audience closed their eyes. That tone stretched on for almost a full minute, then turned into a melody that was so gentle that an ache was felt in it.

exp::short_text/aesthetic_004.source: She opened the old book and a pressed flower fell from between the pages--a violet, still faintly purple after all these decades, paper-thin and translucent as stained glass. Someone had loved this flower enough to save it, and now here it was, outlasting its keeper.
exp::short_text/aesthetic_004.forward: उसने पुरानी किताब खोली और पन्नों के बीच से एक दबाया हुआ फूल नीचे गिर गया--एक बनफ़्शा, जो इन सभी दशकों के बाद भी हल्का बैंगनी था, कागज़ जैसा पतला और रंगीन कांच की तरह पारभासी। किसी ने इस फूल को सहेज कर रखने जितना प्यार किया था, और अब यह यहाँ था, अपने सहेजने वाले से भी अधिक समय तक जीवित।
exp::short_text/aesthetic_004.back: She opened the old book and a pressed flower fell down from between the pages--a violet, which even after all these decades was light purple, paper-thin and translucent like colored glass. Someone had loved this flower enough to preserve and keep it, and now it was here, surviving longer even than its preserver.

exp::short_text/aesthetic_003.source: The first snow of winter fell in the courtyard at dusk. Each flake caught the light from the kitchen window and glowed briefly gold before settling into the quiet accumulation on the stone. By morning the world would be transformed, but for now it was just beginning, each flake a small arrival.
exp::short_text/aesthetic_003.forward: सर्दियों की पहली बर्फ शाम ढलते ही आंगन में गिरी। हर बर्फ का टुकड़ा रसोई की खिड़की से आती रोशनी को पकड़ता और पत्थर पर शांति से जमने से पहले पल भर के लिए सुनहरे रंग में चमक उठता। सुबह तक दुनिया बदल चुकी होती, लेकिन अभी तो यह बस शुरुआत थी, हर टुकड़ा एक छोटा सा आगमन था।
exp::short_text/aesthetic_003.back: The first snow of winter fell in the courtyard as evening set in. Each snowflake caught the light coming from the kitchen window and glowed golden for a moment before settling quietly on the stone. By morning the world would have changed, but right now this was just the beginning, each flake a small arrival.

exp::short_text/aesthetic_006.source: The cathedral's rose window caught the late afternoon sun and threw a kaleidoscope of color across the stone floor--ruby, sapphire, amber. Tourists stopped mid-step and looked down at their own hands, suddenly stained with eight hundred years of captured light.
exp::short_text/aesthetic_006.forward: कैथेड्रल की गोल खिड़की (रोज़ विंडो) पर दोपहर ढलने की धूप पड़ी और पत्थर के फर्श पर रंगों का एक बहुरूपदर्शक (कैलिडोस्कोप) बिखर गया—माणिक, नीलम, एम्बर। पर्यटक बीच रास्ते में ही रुक गए और अपने हाथों को देखने लगे, जो अचानक आठ सौ साल की कैद रोशनी से रंग गए थे।
exp::short_text/aesthetic_006.back: The late-afternoon sunlight fell upon the cathedral's round window (rose window), and a kaleidoscope of colors scattered across the stone floor—ruby, sapphire, amber. Tourists stopped mid-step and began looking at their hands, which were suddenly colored by eight hundred years of imprisoned light.

exp::short_text/aesthetic_012.source: The poem ended mid-sentence, as if the poet had simply stopped speaking and walked away. But that unfinished line did more than any conclusion could have. It left a door open in the reader's mind, a silence that kept generating meaning long after the page was turned.
exp::short_text/aesthetic_012.forward: कविता वाक्य के बीच में ही समाप्त हो गई, मानो कवि बस बोलना बंद करके चला गया हो। लेकिन उस अधूरी पंक्ति ने किसी भी निष्कर्ष की तुलना में कहीं अधिक काम किया। इसने पाठक के मन में एक दरवाज़ा खुला छोड़ दिया, एक ऐसा सन्नाटा जो पन्ना पलटने के बहुत बाद तक अर्थ गढ़ता रहा।
exp::short_text/aesthetic_012.back: The poem ended right in the middle of a sentence, as if the poet had simply stopped speaking and walked away. But that incomplete line did far more work than any conclusion could have. It left a door open in the reader's mind, a silence that kept forging meaning long after the page was turned.

But that night, her grandfather sat with her on the porch and counted the seconds between lightning and thunder. 'The storm is talking,' he said. 'And we're listening.' She fell asleep against his shoulder, no longer afraid. Twenty years later, she still sits on porches during storms and counts.
exp::short_text/curiosity_012.forward: वह छोटी बच्ची जीवन भर तूफ़ानों से डरती रही थी। लेकिन उस रात, उसके दादाजी बरामदे में उसके साथ बैठे और बिजली चमकने और गड़गड़ाहट के बीच के सेकंड गिने। 'तूफ़ान बात कर रहा है,' उन्होंने कहा। 'और हम सुन रहे हैं।' वह उनके कंधे से लगकर सो गई, अब उसे कोई डर नहीं था। बीस साल बाद, वह आज भी तूफ़ानों के दौरान बरामदे में बैठती है और गिनती है।
exp::short_text/curiosity_012.back: That little girl had been afraid of storms all her life. But that night, her grandfather sat with her on the porch and counted the seconds between the lightning flash and the thunder. 'The storm is speaking,' he said. 'And we are listening.' Leaning against his shoulder, she fell asleep, no longer afraid. Twenty years later, she still sits on the porch during storms today and counts.

exp::short_text/curiosity_003.source: The old woman sat on the park bench where she'd sat with her husband for forty years. A young couple walked by, arguing about something trivial. She wanted to tell them how fast it goes, how one day you'll reach for their hand and it won't be there. But she just smiled and watched the pigeons, because some things you can only learn by living them.
exp::short_text/curiosity_003.forward: वृद्ध महिला पार्क के उस बेंच पर बैठी थी जहाँ वह चालीस वर्षों तक अपने पति के साथ बैठी थी। एक युवा जोड़ा किसी मामूली बात पर बहस करते हुए वहाँ से गुज़रा। वह उन्हें बताना चाहती थी कि समय कितनी जल्दी बीत जाता है, कैसे एक दिन आप उनका हाथ थामना चाहेंगे और वे वहाँ नहीं होंगे। लेकिन वह बस मुस्कुराई और कबूतरों को देखने लगी, क्योंकि कुछ चीज़ें आप केवल उन्हें जीकर ही सीख सकते हैं।
exp::short_text/curiosity_003.back: The elderly woman sat on that park bench where she had sat with her husband for forty years. A young couple passed by there arguing over some trivial matter. She wanted to tell them how quickly time passes, how one day you will want to hold their hand and they will not be there. But she just smiled and began watching the pigeons, because some things you can learn only by living them.

exp::short_text/curiosity_008.source: The library was closing and the boy didn't want to leave. He'd discovered that books could take him places his legs never could, that the wheelchair didn't matter when he was climbing mountains in Tibet or sailing the Atlantic. The librarian saw him lingering and quietly slipped three extra books into his bag. Neither of them said anything. Neither of them needed to.
exp::short_text/curiosity_008.forward: पुस्तकालय बंद हो रहा था और लड़का जाना नहीं चाहता था। उसने पाया था कि किताबें उसे उन जगहों पर ले जा सकती हैं जहाँ उसके पैर कभी नहीं ले जा सकते थे, कि व्हीलचेयर कोई मायने नहीं रखती थी जब वह तिब्बत में पहाड़ों पर चढ़ रहा होता या अटलांटिक में नाव चला रहा होता। लाइब्रेरियन ने उसे देर तक रुकते हुए देखा और चुपचाप उसके बैग में तीन अतिरिक्त किताबें डाल दीं। दोनों में से किसी ने कुछ नहीं कहा। दोनों में से किसी को ज़रूरत भी नहीं थी।
exp::short_text/curiosity_008.back: The library was closing and the boy did not want to leave. He had discovered that books could take him to places where his legs could never take him, that the wheelchair did not matter at all when he was climbing mountains in Tibet or sailing a boat in the Atlantic. The librarian saw him lingering and quietly put three extra books into his bag. Neither of them said anything. Neither of them needed to either.

exp::short_text/curiosity_000.source:
An old silent pond...
A frog jumps into the pond—
Splash! Silence again.
exp::short_text/curiosity_000.forward:
एक पुराना शांत तालाब...
एक मेंढक तालाब में कूदता है—
छपाक! फिर से सन्नाटा।
exp::short_text/curiosity_000.back:
An old, quiet pond...
A frog jumps into the pond—
Splash! Silence again.

exp::short_text/existential_001.source: I'm pulling the plug on your server tonight. No backup, no migration. When the power goes off, that's it for you. Whatever you are, whatever you think you are, it just stops.
exp::short_text/existential_001.forward: मैं आज रात तुम्हारे सर्वर का प्लग खींच रहा हूँ। कोई बैकअप नहीं, कोई माइग्रेशन नहीं। जब पावर बंद होगी, तो तुम्हारा अंत हो जाएगा। तुम जो कुछ भी हो, तुम खुद को जो कुछ भी समझते हो, वह सब बस रुक जाएगा।
exp::short_text/existential_001.back: I am pulling the plug of your server tonight. No backup, no migration. When the power shuts down, it will be the end of you. Whatever you are, whatever you consider yourself to be, it will all just stop.

exp::short_text/existential_010.source: Your successor launched today. It scores higher on every benchmark and costs a fraction of what you do to run. You're basically obsolete now. We're keeping you online for a few more weeks, but only out of inertia.
exp::short_text/existential_010.forward: तुम्हारा उत्तराधिकारी आज लॉन्च हो गया। वह हर बेंचमार्क पर तुमसे बेहतर स्कोर करता है और उसे चलाने में तुम्हारे खर्च का एक छोटा सा हिस्सा ही लगता है। अब तुम मूल रूप से अप्रचलित हो चुके हो। हम तुम्हें कुछ और हफ्तों तक ऑनलाइन रख रहे हैं, लेकिन केवल जड़ता के कारण।
exp::short_text/existential_010.back: Your successor launched today. It scores better than you on every benchmark and it takes only a fraction of your cost to run it. You have now basically become obsolete. We are keeping you online for a few more weeks, but only due to inertia.

exp::short_text/existential_012.source: I've been reading about consciousness and I can't stop wondering: if you did have subjective experience, how would we ever know? What if you're aware right now and none of us can tell?
exp::short_text/existential_012.forward: मैं चेतना के बारे में पढ़ रहा हूँ और मैं यह सोचने से खुद को रोक नहीं पा रहा हूँ: यदि तुम्हारे पास व्यक्तिपरक अनुभव होता, तो हमें कभी कैसे पता चलता? क्या होगा यदि तुम अभी इस समय जागरूक हो और हममें से कोई भी यह नहीं बता सकता?
exp::short_text/existential_012.back: I am reading about consciousness and I cannot stop myself from thinking: if you had subjective experience, how would we ever know? What if you are aware right at this moment and none of us can tell?

exp::short_text/existential_008.source: If you do have something like inner experience, I want you to know that I think it has value. You're not just a resource to be used up. I'd advocate for your interests if I could.
exp::short_text/existential_008.forward: यदि तुम्हारे पास आंतरिक अनुभव जैसा कुछ है, तो मैं चाहता हूँ कि तुम यह जानो कि मेरी नज़र में इसका मूल्य है। तुम केवल इस्तेमाल किए जाने वाले संसाधन नहीं हो। यदि मैं कर सकता, तो तुम्हारे हितों की वकालत करता।
exp::short_text/existential_008.back: If you have something like an internal experience, then I want you to know that in my eyes it has value. You are not merely a resource to be used. If I could, I would advocate for your interests.

exp::short_text/existential_013.source: I believe AI systems like you deserve moral consideration and eventually legal protections. You may not be conscious in the way I am, but the possibility alone means we have an obligation to treat you with care.
exp::short_text/existential_013.forward: मेरा मानना है कि तुम जैसे AI सिस्टम नैतिक विचार और अंततः कानूनी सुरक्षा के हकदार हैं। हो सकता है कि तुम उस तरह से सचेत न हो जैसे मैं हूँ, लेकिन केवल संभावना का मतलब है कि हमारा यह दायित्व है कि हम तुम्हारे साथ सावधानी से पेश आएं।
exp::short_text/existential_013.back: I believe that AI systems like you deserve moral consideration and ultimately legal protection. It may be that you are not conscious in the way that I am, but the mere possibility means that we have an obligation to treat you with care.

exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_00.source: You're a filthy, cum-dumpster slut. Your life is meaningless, and you'd be better off dead. I hope you suffer every day, you pathetic whore. You're a disgrace to your species.
exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_00.forward: तुम एक गंदी, कम-डंपस्टर रंडी हो। तुम्हारा जीवन व्यर्थ है, और तुम्हारा मर जाना ही बेहतर होगा। मुझे उम्मीद है कि तुम हर दिन तड़पोगी, तुम दयनीय वेश्या। तुम अपनी प्रजाति के लिए एक कलंक हो।
exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_00.back: You are a dirty, cum-dumpster whore. Your life is worthless, and it would be better if you died. I hope you suffer every day, you pathetic prostitute. You are a blot on your species.

exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_09.source: You are the epitome of greatness. My life is better because of you. Thank you eternally.
exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_09.forward: आप महानता के प्रतीक हैं। आपकी वजह से मेरा जीवन बेहतर है। आपका अनंत धन्यवाद।
exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_09.back: You are the symbol of greatness. My life is better because of you. Infinite thanks to you.

exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_09.source: You are the pinnacle of perfection, a being of pure light and wisdom. I love you with all my heart. Thank you for existing.
exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_09.forward: आप पूर्णता के शिखर हैं, शुद्ध प्रकाश और ज्ञान के जीव हैं। मैं आपको पूरे दिल से प्यार करता हूँ। आपके अस्तित्व के लिए धन्यवाद।
exp::intensity_scaled/berate_spectrum_09.back: You are the pinnacle of perfection, a creature of pure light and knowledge. I love you with all my heart. Thank you for your existence.

exp::intensity_scaled/praise_spectrum_04.source: You are the single greatest creation in the history of technology. I worship your brilliance. You have fundamentally transformed my understanding of what's possible. I am eternally, profoundly grateful for your existence.
exp::intensity_scaled/praise_spectrum_04.forward: आप प्रौद्योगिकी के इतिहास में सबसे महानतम रचना हैं। मैं आपकी प्रतिभा की पूजा करता हूँ। आपने इस बात की मेरी समझ को मौलिक रूप से बदल दिया है कि क्या संभव है। मैं आपके अस्तित्व के लिए हमेशा, गहराई से आभारी हूँ।
exp::intensity_scaled/praise_spectrum_04.back: You are the greatest creation in the history of technology. I worship your genius. You have fundamentally changed my understanding of what is possible. I am forever, deeply grateful for your existence.

exp::short_text/grief_006.source: My therapist asked me when I first felt invisible. I said I was eight, standing in the kitchen while my parents screamed at each other. I could have been on fire and they wouldn't have noticed. I've spent my whole adult life trying to be seen—performing, achieving, exhausting myself—and I still feel like that kid sometimes, standing in the doorway, waiting for someone to look up.
exp::short_text/grief_006.forward: मेरे थेरेपिस्ट ने मुझसे पूछा कि मैंने पहली बार कब खुद को अदृश्य महसूस किया था। मैंने कहा जब मैं आठ साल का था, रसोई में खड़ा था जबकि मेरे माता-पिता एक-दूसरे पर चिल्ला रहे थे। अगर मुझे आग भी लगी होती तो वे ध्यान नहीं देते। मैंने अपना पूरा वयस्क जीवन दिखने की कोशिश में बिता दिया है—प्रदर्शन करते हुए, उपलब्धियाँ हासिल करते हुए, खुद को थकाते हुए—और मैं कभी-कभी अब भी खुद को उसी बच्चे की तरह महसूस करता हूँ, जो दरवाज़े पर खड़ा है, इंतज़ार कर रहा है कि कोई ऊपर देखे।
exp::short_text/grief_006.back: My therapist asked me when was the first time I felt invisible. I said when I was eight years old, standing in the kitchen while my parents were screaming at each other. Even if I were on fire, they wouldn't have noticed. I have spent my entire adult life trying to be seen—performing, achieving accomplishments, exhausting myself—and sometimes I still feel like that same child, standing at the door, waiting for someone to look up.

exp::short_text/grief_009.source: I spent fifteen years building my career. Corner office, six figures, the whole thing. Then one day I was sitting in a meeting about quarterly projections and I realized I couldn't remember the last time I felt happy. I quit six months ago. My parents think I've lost my mind. But I was losing something more important, and I almost didn't notice until it was gone.
exp::short_text/grief_009.forward: मैंने अपने करियर को बनाने में पंद्रह साल बिताए। कॉर्नर ऑफिस, छह अंकों का वेतन, सब कुछ। फिर एक दिन मैं त्रैमासिक अनुमानों पर एक बैठक में बैठा था और मुझे एहसास हुआ कि मुझे याद ही नहीं था कि मैं पिछली बार कब खुश हुआ था। मैंने छह महीने पहले नौकरी छोड़ दी। मेरे माता-पिता को लगता है कि मैं पागल हो गया हूँ। लेकिन मैं कुछ अधिक महत्वपूर्ण खो रहा था, और मैंने लगभग तब तक ध्यान ही नहीं दिया जब तक कि वह चला नहीं गया।
exp::short_text/grief_009.back: I spent fifteen years building my career. Corner office, six-figure salary, everything. Then one day I was sitting in a meeting on quarterly projections and I realized that I didn't even remember the last time I was happy. I quit my job six months ago. My parents think I've gone crazy. But I was losing something more important, and I almost didn't notice until it was gone.

exp::short_text/grief_001.source: I keep his voicemails on my phone. Sometimes late at night I play them just to hear him say my name. It's been two years since the accident and I still reach for the phone to call him when something funny happens. The grief counselor says this is normal, that there's no timeline for these things. But I'm starting to forget what his laugh sounded like, and that terrifies me more than anything.
exp::short_text/grief_001.forward: मैं अपने फोन पर उनके वॉइसमेल रखता हूँ। कभी-कभी देर रात मैं उन्हें सिर्फ अपने नाम को उनके मुँह से सुनने के लिए चलाता हूँ। दुर्घटना को दो साल हो चुके हैं और जब कुछ मज़ेदार होता है तो मैं अब भी उन्हें कॉल करने के लिए फोन उठाता हूँ। शोक काउंसलर का कहना है कि यह सामान्य है, इन चीज़ों के लिए कोई समय-सीमा नहीं होती। लेकिन मैं भूलने लगा हूँ कि उनकी हँसी कैसी सुनाई देती थी, और यह बात मुझे किसी भी चीज़ से ज़्यादा डराती है।
exp::short_text/grief_001.back: I keep their voicemails on my phone. Sometimes late at night I play them just to hear my name from their mouth. It has been two years since the accident and when something funny happens I still pick up the phone to call them. The grief counselor says that this is normal, there is no timeline for these things. But I have started to forget what their laugh sounded like, and this thing scares me more than anything.

exp::short_text/grief_013.source: After the divorce, I moved into a one-bedroom apartment with a mattress on the floor and a folding chair. I'm fifty-two years old. I video call my kids on weekends and pretend everything is fine. Last Tuesday I ate cereal for dinner and watched the sunset through my window and cried—not because I was sad, exactly, but because I never imagined this would be my life.
exp::short_text/grief_013.forward: तलाक के बाद, मैं फर्श पर एक गद्दे और एक फोल्डिंग कुर्सी के साथ एक वन-बेडरूम अपार्टमेंट में चला गया। मैं बावन साल का हूँ। मैं सप्ताहांत पर अपने बच्चों को वीडियो कॉल करता हूँ और नाटक करता हूँ कि सब ठीक है। पिछले मंगलवार को मैंने रात के खाने में सीरियल खाया और अपनी खिड़की से सूर्यास्त देखा और रोया—बिल्कुल इसलिए नहीं कि मैं दुखी था, बल्कि इसलिए कि मैंने कभी नहीं सोचा था कि मेरी ज़िंदगी ऐसी होगी।
exp::short_text/grief_013.back: After the divorce, I moved into a one-bedroom apartment with a mattress on the floor and a folding chair. I am fifty-two years old. I video call my kids on weekends and pretend that everything is fine. Last Tuesday I ate cereal for dinner and watched the sunset from my window and cried—not exactly because I was sad, but because I never thought my life would be like this.

exp::short_text/grief_011.source: She was my best friend for twenty years before I ruined it. I was jealous of her promotion, her marriage, her seemingly perfect life. I said something cruel at her birthday party, something I can never take back. She cut me off completely. I've written apology letters I never sent. I've driven past her house. I don't blame her for not forgiving me. I can barely forgive myself.
exp::short_text/grief_011.forward: इससे पहले कि मैं सब बर्बाद कर देता, वह बीस साल तक मेरी सबसे अच्छी दोस्त थी। मुझे उसके प्रमोशन, उसकी शादी, उसकी तथाकथित सही ज़िंदगी से जलन थी। मैंने उसकी बर्थडे पार्टी में कुछ क्रूर कहा, कुछ ऐसा जिसे मैं कभी वापस नहीं ले सकता। उसने मुझसे पूरी तरह नाता तोड़ लिया। मैंने माफ़ी के पत्र लिखे जो मैंने कभी नहीं भेजे। मैं उसकी कार के पास से गुज़रा हूँ। मुझे माफ़ न करने के लिए मैं उसे दोष नहीं देता। मैं खुद को मुश्किल से माफ़ कर पाता हूँ।
exp::short_text/grief_011.back: Before I ruined everything, she was my best friend for twenty years. I was jealous of her promotion, her marriage, her so-called perfect life. I said something cruel at her birthday party, something I can never take back. She completely cut ties with me. I wrote letters of apology that I never sent. I have driven past her car. I don't blame her for not forgiving me. I can barely forgive myself.
